response.message: Astra: Your suggestion to explore another sense has a foothold already: the birds’ calls. “Joyful” gives them a mood, but little audible character. What would Whisker hear from inside their circling that a distant observer might miss? Try a brief listening passage rather than another whole-scene revision. Spend attention where the sound makes her situation more particular; stop when extra description only repeats the mood. You can decide whether the experiment earns a place in the story.
response.rationale: After two repetitive drafts, shift to a concrete auditory experiment within Whisker’s scene, connecting selective attention with independent editorial judgment.
